To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

MelB is a 12-transmembrane domain (TM) protein with a topology similar to other bacterial secondary carriers and that the interaction of melibiose with MelB in the presence of Na+, Li+, or H+ induces conformational changes in the cytoplamic loops of MelB.

the topology of the melibiose transport protein MelB from Escherichia coil has been determined, that the cytoplamic domain of MelB is accessible to protease digestion and that melibiose binding induces a conformational change in MelB that is detected by the increased resistance of the protein to protease digestion.
the cytoplamic loops connecting transmembranes 4-5 and 6-7 are exposed in the inner membrane and are accessible to protease digestion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the mechanism of action of a bacterial sugar transporter, MelB.
the identification of the cation- and melibiose-binding site(s) of Mel B, as well as the conformational change of MelB induced by the interaction of both cosubstrates.
the identification and mapping of the cytoplamsic loops of the MelB permease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MelB is an 11-transmembrane protein with the carboxy terminus exposed in the cytosol and the amino terminus exposed in periplasm.
the topology of MelB is consistent with the 12 transmembrane domain model.
MelB undergoes a conformational change upon interaction with the cosubstrates Na+ or Li+, and melibiose.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the topology of MelB is similar to that of the lactose permease of E. coli, and the presence of melibiose plus Na+ or Li+, but not melibiose alone, results in conformational changes of the cytoplASMic loops of MelB.
loop 4/5 is near or in the cation-binding site, loop 10/11 and the carboxyl terminus are in the cytoplamic side of the membrane, and loops 5/6 and 7/8 are in the periplasmic side of the membrane.

the topology of MelB is similar to that of other secondary transporters, with the cytoplasmically exposed regions being more susceptible to proteases and with the periplasmic regions being more resistant.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the topology of MelB and the effect of melibiose binding on the conformation of the protein are similar to that of other bacterial Na+ (Li+) symporters, such as LacY and GlcT, but different from the Na+-dependent H+ antiporter NhaA.
the topology of MelB is consistent with the current models of the secondary structure of MelB.
the topology of MelB is consistent with that of a 12-transmembrane helix transporter.
